title: Metric overrides
description: What writers add to the generated metrics data. An override is a stopgap or enrichment. A stopgap stands in for something the tooling should produce: a better description than the help string in Redpanda, or the labels of a metric the metrics cluster did not export. The release run deletes a stopgap as soon as the tooling produces the same thing. Enrichment is what no tool can produce: text for one audience, Cloud availability, links, sections and usage guidance. A run with --retire-overrides also deletes an override whole when the source at the release being generated no longer registers its metric and the dataset of an earlier release in --dataset-dir has it. Without such a dataset the override is kept and reported, because its metric may be for a release that is not out yet. An override for a metric that is still in source and has a written reason for not being exported is kept and reported too. doc-tools generate metrics-docs --overrides merges this file into redpanda-metrics-<tag>.json.

_comment.description: A note for other writers. Not copied into the data.

description.description: Text for readers. A stopgap: it replaces the help string from Redpanda, which stays in the data as source_description, and it is deleted when the help string in a release says the same. Fix the help string in the Redpanda source and name that change in upstream_ref. An array of paragraphs when one belongs to a single docs build: an entry may start with 'cloud-only:' or 'self-managed-only:'. Audience paragraphs are enrichment and are never deleted.

upstream_ref.description: The issue or pull request against the Redpanda source that will make the description override redundant, as 'redpanda-data/streaming-enterprise#12345' or a URL. Set it so the override has a way out. Deleted together with the description.

unit.description: Unit of the value, when the name does not say it. A stopgap: deleted when the tooling gives the same unit.

labels.description: For a metric the cluster exported: a description and the complete values of labels it has, which is enrichment and stays. For a metric the cluster did not export: its labels, read from the source file the gap report names. Giving this list, even an empty one, covers that gap. That part is a stopgap: once the cluster exports the metric, a label entry with only a name is deleted, and so is an entry for a label the cluster does not have.

values.description: The complete set of values the label can take.

use_cases.description: What a reader would use the metric for. Drives the catalog filter.

usage.description: How to use the metric, as AsciiDoc.

availability.description: Deployment -> whether the metric is available there.

requires.description: What a cluster needs before it exports the metric. A stopgap for a metric the tooling does not know about yet: it replaces the list from the tooling, and is deleted when the tooling gives the same list.
